subject: Re: Content safeguards — SLA scope, runtime routing and temporary mitigation
messages:
From: FinBank Security Team <security@finbank.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@finbank.com>, Emily Shaw <emily.shaw@finbank.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Impact of content safeguards on tool-calling latency — request for temporary scope adjustment

Hannah,

Thanks for the recent rollout notes. Over the last 48 hours we observed a spike in failed tool-calling handoffs and structured-output validation rejections against our production integration. These failures are manifesting as increased 95th-percentile CPU-bound latencies on our side and several user-facing transaction timeouts.

Example symptoms:
- Tool-call invocations returning 500s when content-safeguard check triggered (attached log snippet).
- Structured output validation returning schema mismatches that cause downstream order processing to abort.
- Intermittent additional 200–400ms processing per request when the runtime routes through the new moderation micro-path.

We understand safety policies are critical. For FinBank’s payments flow we need an agreed mitigation: either a temporary SLA carve-out defining acceptable error/latency windows for the moderation flow, or a guaranteed alternative routing policy that keeps the main payment path within our 99th percentile latency SLO.

Can Redwood propose a scoped plan (timeboxed) that includes:
1) a list of impacted endpoints and expected failure modes,
2) an emergency routing policy that minimizes latency impact for high-value transactions, and
3) proposed compensation/credits if latency-calibrated SLOs are missed during the mitigation window.

We’d like to resolve this by end of day Monday PST. Happy to hop on a quick call — suggest 10am Mon.

Thanks,
Security Team
FinBank

--
FinBank Security Team
security@finbank.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: FinBank Security Team <security@finbank.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 17:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Impact of content safeguards on tool-calling latency — request for temporary scope adjustment

Raj / FinBank Security Team —

Thanks for the detailed report and the log snippet. We take production regressions seriously. I’ve looped in Markus (VP Product) and Grace (Customer Solutions) to coordinate an urgent response.

Quick summary of next steps from Redwood:
- Internal triage to identify the exact moderation rule triggering the additional runtime path (Diego will lead).
- Proposal for a temporary routing policy that pins payment-critical routes to the low-latency path and uses a conservative moderation pass asynchronously.
- A short SLA addendum draft that scopes an exception window and defines compensation/credits if our adjusted 99th/95th latencies are exceeded.

We’ll have an initial mitigation proposal by COB Monday. In the meantime, can you confirm the list of endpoint paths you classify as "payment-critical" (ok to paste a short list)? That will let Diego size the routing rules.

I’ve attached an internal SLA matrix and a runtime routing diagram for reference.

Best,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_sla_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), runtime-routing-diagram.png (image)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, FinBank Security Team <security@finbank.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 13 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Impact of content safeguards on tool-calling latency — request for temporary scope adjustment

Team / Raj —

I support Hannah’s path: triage, temporary routing, and a timeboxed SLA addendum. A few principles from the product side:
- Any carve-out must be explicit (endpoints, duration, metrics) and have automated rollback.
- We should avoid permanent weakening of safety rules; this is a targeted operational mitigation.
- Compensation should be proportional and defined as credits against next billing cycle; legal will draft language but we can propose numbers.

Grace — please draft a short addendum that:
1) lists payment-critical endpoints (we'll populate if FinBank provides),
2) defines the monitoring windows and thresholds (95th/99th latency targets), and
3) suggests credit bands for missed buckets.

Hannah — once Grace has a draft, we’ll run it by Diego for technical feasibility and by legal for terms.

Markus
VP Product, Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, FinBank Security Team <security@finbank.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 08:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Impact of content safeguards on tool-calling latency — request for temporary scope adjustment

Raj / team —

I dug into the logs you sent (thanks). The failures correlate with two guardrail checks that push requests into the moderation micro-path: a heuristics-based ngram block and a structured-output schema validator that re-runs a second pass. The extra 200–400ms is mostly from serialization + sync validation.

Mitigation options (quick tech summary):
A) Fast-path routing: detect payment-critical route at the edge and bypass synchronous moderation, instead writing an async inspection log and queuing a downstream verification job. This keeps p99 latency under target but raises a small eventual-consistency window for flagged content.
B) Lightweight sync-check: replace the heavy schema validator with a faster JSON-schema prefilter that drops only clearly malformed outputs. This reduces errors but still keeps a sync step.
C) Hybrid: fast-path for specific endpoints, lightweight sync for lower-risk flows.

Estimated timeline:
- A: 8–12 hours of engineering work + immediate feature flag.
- B: 4–6 hours to implement a prefilter rule and test in staging.
- C: 1 business day to put both in place with thorough monitoring.

I recommend option C as a balanced approach. We can implement a feature-flagged fast-path tonight and flip it on for the endpoints you mark as payment-critical. We’ll stream extra logs to the FinBank security bucket and set up alerting on error-rates and schema-rejection rates.

Attaching a short failure log extract in case it helps: finbank_toolcall-failure-log-snippet.txt

Diego
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: FinBank Security Team <security@finbank.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 11:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Impact of content safeguards on tool-calling latency — request for temporary scope adjustment

Raj / Emily —

Thanks for the prompt escalation and for the export. Summary of agreement and next steps:
1) Scope: FinBank confirms the following payment-critical endpoints: /payments/charge, /payments/settle, /payments/refund. These will be placed on a fast-path routing policy.
2) Technical mitigation: Redwood will implement the hybrid plan (option C). We will deploy a feature-flagged fast-path tonight for the three endpoints and enable a JSON prefilter on related lower-risk routes.
3) Monitoring & evidence: Redwood will stream detailed moderation and tool-call logs to the FinBank S3 bucket and provide a shared dashboard (link in Drive).
4) SLA addendum: Grace will produce an addendum that:
   - defines the carve-out period (start: 2026-06-14 20:00 UTC, max duration 14 days),
   - enumerates the metrics (p95/p99 latency targets for the main path), and
   - specifies credit bands if targets are missed.
5) Rollback & safety: The change is feature-flagged with automatic rollback if error-rate for structured-output failures increases by >2x baseline.

Action items:
- FinBank: confirm endpoints above (Raj/Emily) and provide any additional critical routes by 17:00 PST today.
- Grace: draft SLA addendum and proposed credit bands (ETA 18:00 PST today).
- Diego: implement feature-flagged fast-path tonight and confirm deployment + logs.

We will also prepare a brief customer-facing note that describes the temporary scope without exposing internal guardrail details. I’ll coordinate with legal if FinBank wants formal DocuSign signatures — I included a provisional link to an addendum template.

Hannah
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_sla_matrix_v2.xlsx, runtime-routing-diagram.png, finbank_toolcall-failure-log-snippet.txt
